items.title: Finite power series and fourth-order derivative budgets

source.anchor: iteratedDeriv_pow and the finite-sum iterated-derivative interface
source.attribution: Mathlib supplies the monomial derivative identity; Samplinglib packages finite supports, signed coefficient budgets, and the fourth-order scalar estimate.

items.statement: A finite real power series is smooth, has the expected descending-factorial derivative formula at every order, and admits an absolute coefficient bound on the unit interval; the same elementary estimates control the scalar fourth-order composition expression.
assumptions: The exponent support is finite and coefficients are arbitrary real numbers.
The derivative budget is evaluated at a point with absolute value at most one.
The fourth-order estimate assumes separate absolute bounds for the first four outer derivatives.

obligations.label: Define the finite series and its closed derivative expressions
Prove smoothness and the exact arbitrary-order derivative formula
Bound every iterated derivative on the unit interval
Control the scalar fourth-order composition expression term by term

bindings.boundary: No canonical support or infinite-series statement is asserted.

items.title: Explicit geodesics and exponential maps on the unit sphere

source.edition: An Introduction to Optimization on Smooth Manifolds, 2023
source.anchor: sphere geometry, geodesics, and the Riemannian exponential map
source.attribution: Nicolas Boumal for the geometric route; Samplinglib supplies the ambient Hilbert-space formulas and explicit fourth-order analytic bounds.

items.statement: In a real inner-product space, the standard trigonometric curve gives the signed unit-sphere geodesic. It is smooth, agrees with the ambient exponential formula at nonnegative time, preserves unit norm for tangent increments, and has explicit derivatives and uniform bounds through order four.
assumptions: The ambient space is a real normed additive commutative group with an inner product.
Norm preservation assumes a unit base point and an orthogonal tangent increment.
The displayed closed derivative bundle assumes nonzero velocity; zero velocity is the constant curve.

obligations.label: Define the exponential formula and signed geodesic
Identify forward geodesic time with scaled exponential input
Verify exact derivatives and bounds through order four
Prove that tangent increments remain on the unit sphere

bindings.boundary: Without unit length and tangency, unit norm is not asserted.
